title: Birth of Modern Alpinism: Mont Blanc
summary: Universally recognized as the inception of modern mountaineering, dispelling centuries of medieval superstition that high peaks were inhabited by demons.

title: Conquest of the Matterhorn
summary: Concluded the Victorian 'Golden Age of Alpinism'. Triumph was overshadowed by tragedy when a snapped Manila hemp rope sent four climbers falling 1,400 meters.

title: Everest Reconnaissance & The Mallory Enigma
summary: Last sighted 'going strong for the top' near the Second Step clad in tweed jackets and rudimentary oxygen sets, sparking the enduring question of mountaineering history.

title: First 8,000m Summit: Annapurna I
summary: The first human footsteps on an eight-thousander, accomplished without bottled oxygen. Herzog famously declared: 'There are other Annapurnas in the lives of men.'

title: First Summit of Mount Everest
summary: Standing atop the planet's highest pinnacle at 11:30 AM on May 29 via the South Col and Hillary Step, securing immortal global acclaim.

title: First Ascent of K2 (The Savage Mountain)
climbers: Achille Compagnoni & Lino Lacedelli (with Walter Bonatti & Amir Mehdi)
summary: Conquered Earth's steepest giant via the Abruzzi Spur after Walter Bonatti and Hunza high-altitude porter Amir Mehdi survived an open bivouac at 8,100m.

title: Everest Without Bottled Oxygen
summary: Shattered scientific dogma by proving human respiration is physiologically possible in the Death Zone without artificial supplemental oxygen.

title: The First Crown of All 14 Eight-Thousanders
summary: Messner completed all 14 summits over sixteen years, pioneering pure alpine style, lightweight gear, and zero supplemental oxygen.

title: Historic First Winter Ascent of K2
climbers: 10-Climber All-Nepali Team (Led by Nirmal Purja & Mingma G)
summary: Solved the 'Last Great Problem' of world mountaineering at -60°C and hurricane gusts, stepping onto the summit together arm-in-arm.

title: Youngest to Summit All 14 Peaks: Nima Rinji
summary: Completed the full 14 Eight-Thousanders crown at just 18 years old, ushering in the modern era of next-generation Himalayan high-altitude athletes.
